name: 16g replay exposure
title: Replay exposure over a 20B-token run
subtitle: Domain corpus: 8B unique tokens of filings and 2B of call transcripts; replay ratio 25%

steps.caption: A replay ratio of 25% gives 5B of the 20B tokens to general text and leaves 15B for the domain.
Transcripts get 25% of the domain share, more than their 20% of the domain text, so they are read 1.875 times while the filings are read 1.41 times.
Each step reads 512 windows of 4,096 tokens: 128 general, 96 transcript and 288 filing windows. The run takes 9,537 such steps.
The 5B replay tokens follow the original pretraining mixture: 3.6B web, 0.8B code, 0.3B books, 0.2B papers and 0.1B Wikipedia. That is 0.25% of the 2T tokens, so almost all of it is fresh.
With no replay the same 20B tokens read the domain 2.0 times, with 50% replay 1.0 times. Holding domain exposure at 15B instead costs 15B, 20B or 30B tokens, a factor of 1 / (1 - r).
